lessons.title: Comparing Two Non-Fiction Texts
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare information from two non-fiction texts about different places.
success_criteria: I can find a fact from each text.
I can compare them.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap facts about the village and our own local area.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model comparing facts from a text about the village and a text about our own local area.
lessons.independent_task: Children compare facts from both texts, recording similarities and differences.
resources_needed: Village and local area non-fiction texts
key_questions: What is similar about the two places?

differentiation.support: Compare with adult support, one similarity/difference

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comparative comprehension across two non-fiction texts — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Tell your family one similarity between the two places.

lessons.title: Comparing Data: Two Localities
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare data between two localities in a table.
success_criteria: I can complete a comparison table.
I can answer a question about it.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the comparison table format from Week 10.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model organising facts about both localities into a comparison table (population, climate, homes).
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a comparison table for the two localities and answer questions.

differentiation.greater_depth: Add extra rows and answer detailed questions

lessons.assessment_notes: Note data organisation skill applied to a geography comparison — evidence for MATHS.STAT.
lessons.home_link: Make a comparison table about two places you know.

lessons.title: Similarities Between Our Locality and the Village
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify similarities between the two localities.
success_criteria: I can name a similarity.
I can explain why it's similar.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model identifying genuine similarities (e.g. both have schools, families, shops/markets) between the localities.
lessons.independent_task: Children record similarities between their own locality and the village.
resources_needed: Facts and pictures from both localities
lessons.assessment_notes: Note geographical comparison skill, focusing on similarities to avoid stereotyping — evidence for GEOG.1.
lessons.home_link: Think of another similarity with your family.

lessons.title: Using 'And' and 'But' to Compare Localities
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to use coordinating conjunctions to compare the two localities.
success_criteria: I can use 'and' to join similar ideas.
I can use 'but' to join different ideas.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model using 'and' for similarities and 'but' for differences between the localities.
lessons.independent_task: Children write comparison sentences using 'and' and 'but'.

differentiation.greater_depth: Write 4+ varied sentences using both conjunctions

lessons.assessment_notes: Note use of coordinating conjunctions — evidence for ENG.W3.
lessons.plenary: Share comparison sentences with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Make up a sentence using 'and' or 'but' comparing two places.

lessons.title: Fractions: Comparing Proportions
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to use fraction language to compare proportions between localities.
success_criteria: I can say 'about half' or 'about a quarter'.
I can use this to compare data.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model using fraction language to describe proportions (e.g. 'about half the homes here are...').
lessons.independent_task: Children use fraction language to describe and compare proportions from the week's data.

differentiation.greater_depth: Use fraction language independently and accurately

lessons.assessment_notes: Note application of fractions to real comparative data — evidence for MATHS.N4.
lessons.home_link: Use fraction language to describe something at home.

lessons.title: Differences Between Our Locality and the Village
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify differences between the two localities.
success_criteria: I can name a difference.
I can explain why it might be different.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model identifying genuine differences (e.g. climate, types of homes, transport) between the localities.
lessons.independent_task: Children record differences between their own locality and the village, with reasoning.
resources_needed: Facts and pictures from both localities
key_questions: What is different about the two places?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note geographical comparison skill, handled sensitively without value judgements — evidence for GEOG.1.
lessons.home_link: Think of another difference with your family.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Comparison Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read comparison words fluently.
success_criteria: I can read comparison words.
I can read a comparison sentence.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Reinforce a spelling pattern, applying it to comparison words (e.g. 'same', 'different', 'both').
lessons.independent_task: Children read comparison sentence cards about the two localities.
key_questions: Can you read this comparison sentence?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics/spelling application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading comparison words over the week.

lessons.title: Locality Word Problems
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve word problems comparing quantities from two localities.
success_criteria: I can compare two quantities.
I can solve the problem.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving word problems comparing quantities between the two localities (e.g. rainfall, population size represented simply).
lessons.independent_task: Children solve comparison word problems within 100, showing working.
key_questions: What is the difference between these numbers?
How did you work it out?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record comparison word problem solving skill — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.home_link: Make up a comparison word problem for your family.

lessons.title: Would You Like to Live There? Discussion
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to discuss aspects of the village they find interesting.
success_criteria: I can say something interesting about the village.
I can explain why it interests me.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap all learning about the village so far.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model discussing an interesting aspect of the village respectfully, avoiding value judgements about 'better' or 'worse'.
lessons.independent_task: Children discuss and record an aspect of the village they find interesting, with reasoning.
resources_needed: Village facts and pictures from the two weeks
key_questions: What do you find interesting about the village?

differentiation.greater_depth: Give detailed reasoning for their interest

lessons.assessment_notes: Note respectful, curious engagement with a contrasting locality, avoiding stereotyping — evidence for GEOG.1.
lessons.home_link: Share an interesting fact about the village with your family.

lessons.title: Presenting Our Locality Comparison
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to present a comparison of the two localities clearly.
success_criteria: I can present a similarity and a difference.
I can answer a question about it.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss what makes a clear presentation of a geographical comparison.
lessons.independent_task: Children present their locality comparison to a small group, answering a question.

differentiation.greater_depth: Present unprompted with confidence and detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note spoken language and geographical comparison skill — evidence for ENG.SL1/GEOG.1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate all the locality comparisons presented.
lessons.home_link: Present your locality comparison to your family.

lessons.title: Position and Direction: Where Is the Village?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to use positional language to describe the village's location relative to the UK.
success_criteria: I can say which direction the village is from the UK.
I can use positional language.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model using positional/compass language to describe India's location relative to the UK on a world map.
lessons.independent_task: Children describe the village's location relative to the UK using compass directions.
key_questions: Is India north or south of the UK?

differentiation.support: Use simple positional words with support
differentiation.greater_depth: Use compass directions confidently and accurately

lessons.assessment_notes: Note cross-curricular application of positional language to a world map — evidence for MATHS.GEO.
lessons.plenary: Recap the village's position relative to the UK.
lessons.home_link: Describe the position of a place relative to another using a map.

lessons.title: Making a Comparison Poster
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to present a comparison of the two localities visually.
success_criteria: I can include facts about both localities.
I can show a similarity and difference.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap all facts gathered about both localities.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model designing a comparison poster with sections for each locality and shared facts.
lessons.independent_task: Children create a comparison poster about their own locality and the village.
key_questions: What will you include for each locality?
How will you show what they share?

differentiation.greater_depth: Include detailed facts and a personal reflection section

lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis and presentation of comparative geographical knowledge — evidence for GEOG.1.
lessons.home_link: Show your poster to your family and explain the comparisons.

lessons.title: Comparing Localities Quiz: Reading Comprehension
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions comparing the two localities.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question.
I can answer an inference question.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a summary passage comparing the two localities, modelling retrieval and inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and inference questions about the passage.
key_questions: Why might homes look different in each place?

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family comparing the two localities.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Comparison Data and Number
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply comparison, data and number skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can compare data in a table.
I can solve comparison word problems.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of the week's comparison, data, and number learning.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 2 stations: data comparison, word problems.
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 19 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.STAT/N2.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining both skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising comparison problems over the weekend.

lessons.title: Contrasting Locality Topic Recap and Celebration
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key learning from the contrasting locality study.
success_criteria: I can name a similarity between the two places.
I can name a difference.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss synthesising the two weeks' learning comparing localities.
lessons.independent_task: Children contribute to a final class display celebrating the contrasting locality study.
key_questions: What have we learned by comparing these two places?
lessons.assessment_notes: End of contrasting locality unit consolidation summary for each child — evidence for GEOG.1.
lessons.plenary: Unveil the finished contrasting locality display, celebrating two weeks of geography learning.
lessons.home_link: Share everything you learned about the two localities with your family.
